Develop multi-agent systems and AI copilots that streamline campaign ideation, execution, and performance reporting.   Collaborate with Applied Scientists to develop machine learning-powered features, including audience optimization and incrementality measurement.   Build monitoring and alerting infrastructure to ensure high availability and reliability of marketing operations.   Contribute to system design, architecture decisions, and code reviews to improve software quality, scalability, and reliability. Preferred Qualifications     Experience developing AI-native systems.   Familiarity with agentic frameworks and Amazon Bedrock.   Experience with advertising technology platforms and campaign management systems.   Familiarity with AWS Clean Rooms.   Experience with TypeScript.       Ampcus is an Equal Opportunity Employer. https://job-boards.greenhouse.io/thetrad:
The Trade Desk is a global technology company and the world’s leading independent platform for digital advertising, with over 3,000 employees across more than 30 offices. Our technology helps advertisers reach the right audiences across the open internet — from streaming TV and podcasts to mobile apps, news, and more.
Advertising powers the content people love. By making it more transparent, effective, and responsible, we help support trusted journalism, quality entertainment, and creators worldwide. The world’s brands and agencies rely on us to reach their customers and grow their businesses responsibly.
The scale of our platform brings unique technical challenges — from processing massive datasets in real time to building systems that operate reliably on a global scale. When you work here, your impact is worldwide. We welcome diverse perspectives, encourage curiosity, and build teams that learn from one another. If you’re driven to solve meaningful challenges, we’d love to meet you.
What we do:
Every engineer at The Trade Desk uses the security tools you will build. As a Security Software Engineer you will build and maintain the applications behind our security program, including our developer portal and vulnerability management interface. You will write production code, ship features that engineers actually use, and help turn security data into something developers can act on without opening a ticket.
This is a software engineering role on a security team. You will work alongside security engineers, platform engineers, and product engineering teams, and you will have a senior engineer to learn from.
What you'll do:
Build features across the stack for internal security applications: UI, services, APIs, and data models.
Integrate data from scanners, source control, CI/CD, cloud inventory, and ticketing into one view of risk, mapped to the teams that own each service.
Write unit, integration, and end-to-end tests, and take part in code review.
Help run what we ship: monitor services, join the on-call rotation, and fix bugs and vulnerabilities in the code you own.
Talk with engineers who use our tools, learn what slows them down, and turn it into improvements.
Keep documentation and runbooks current.
Who you are:
2 to 4 years of professional software engineering experience, or equivalent.
Proficiency in at least one backend language we use, such as C#, .NET, Python, Go, or Java.
Experience building web applications or APIs, including some frontend work (React or similar).
Experience with automated testing, Git, and CI/CD.
Working knowledge of a cloud platform (AWS, Azure, or GCP) and containers.
Curiosity about security and a willingness to learn it on the job. Prior security experience is welcome but not required.
Clear written and verbal communication.
Nice to have:
Experience on internal tools, developer experience, or platform teams.
Familiarity with Backstage or another developer portal or software catalog.
Exposure to vulnerability data (CVE, CVSS), SAST/SCA tooling, or secure coding practices such as the OWASP Top 10.
Experience with infrastructure as code (Terraform).
Contributions to open source projects.
A security certification or a security degree is not required.
Prior work on a security team is not required.
